title: The Small Garden
premise: Emrys Reyes, a pastry chef drowning in debt, agrees to a fake date with festival organizer Julian Ashford to survive her family's reunion — but the arrangement entangles them both in a land-grab scheme threatening the community garden that anchors their neighborhood. As Emrys fights to save her café and the garden, she must confront the guilt of abandoning her late mother's dream and forgive herself for choosing survival over love once before. When Julian's family is revealed as the developers, Emrys must choose between the security he offers and the truth she owes herself. In the end, the garden blooms on its own terms: the café survives through community ownership, and Emrys and Julian begin again — slowly, honestly, without contracts.
about_author: Xanthe Sterling is a former line cook who traded kitchen heat for the quieter warmth of love stories set in small businesses and stubborn communities. She writes about people who bake their feelings into things because saying them out loud is harder.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Opening in the pre-dawn hours of her failing café, Emrys counts invoices and swears off romance as an unaffordable luxury. Emotional beat: weary defiance masking fear.

chapters.title: The Reunion Letter
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Her mother's sister summons the family to the harvest reunion, where Emrys's 'success' will be measured against cousins. Beat: dread and old shame resurfacing.

chapters.title: A Man at Table Six
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Julian notices Emrys defending a regular from a landlord's agent; he's in town scouting for his family's development firm. Beat: reluctant admiration.

chapters.title: An Indecent Proposal, Lightly Frosted
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. Julian offers to be her fake date for the reunion if she'll show him the neighborhood. Beat: wary negotiation, sparks under sarcasm.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. They draft rules over day-old croissants: no real feelings, no lies beyond necessity. Beat: playful tension with an undertow of loneliness.

chapters.title: The Garden at the End of the Block
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Emrys shows him the community garden her mother helped found; he photographs it for 'research' he doesn't fully explain. Beat: wonder shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: Meeting the Reyes Women
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The reunion begins; Julian charms her aunts while Emrys endures comparisons to her cousin's corporate success. Beat: humiliation softened by unexpected loyalty.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys brings her signature tart; Julian defends her work when a relative sneers, and their hands touch reaching for the same plate. Beat: the fake cracks.

chapters.title: Driving Home in Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Neither speaks on the drive back, both replaying the moment. Beat: terrified hope.

chapters.title: Eviction Notice, Garden Edition
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Notices appear: the garden lot is slated for demolition by Ashford Development. Beat: betrayal before she knows the source.

chapters.title: The Name on the Letterhead
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Julian realizes his family is behind both the garden seizure and pressure on Emrys's landlord. Beat: complicity and nausea.

chapters.title: What He Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys discovers Julian's surname connection via a newspaper clipping. Beat: cold fury colliding with grief.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Walk-In
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A frozen-cold argument among the freezers: he confesses the job but claims he came to stop it. Beat: trust shattered, not ended.

chapters.title: Mother's Notebook
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Going through her mother's things, Emrys finds plans for the garden — and a letter admitting she chose the garden over being present for Emrys. Beat: inherited wounds.

chapters.title: The Mirror Chapter
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Alone, Emrys admits she abandoned her own dream once, taking the safe corporate job that let the café decay. Beat: the beginning of self-forgiveness.

chapters.title: Julian Resigns
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Julian confronts his father, offers his resignation, and is cut off financially and emotionally. Beat: liberation priced in loss.

chapters.title: Organizing the Harvest
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts. Neighbors rally to save the garden; Emrys reluctantly becomes its spokesperson. Beat: purpose replacing paralysis.

chapters.title: Catering the Cause
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys bakes for the fundraiser; Julian shows up to haul tables, unpaid. Beat: grudging thaw.

chapters.title: Rain on the Tent Roof
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Trapped under a collapsing tent during a storm, they finally talk honestly about fear and failure. Beat: intimacy through vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Almost Kiss
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Under the awning, faces close — interrupted by a neighbor's emergency. Beat: suspended longing.

chapters.title: His Father's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Julian POV. The senior Ashford fast-tracks permits and leaks that Julian fed him information. Beat: public ruin of Julian's reputation.

chapters.title: The Headline
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys reads the story painting Julian as a spy; the neighborhood turns on him. Beat: doubt rekindled despite everything.

chapters.title: Empty Café, Full Heart
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Business booms from fundraiser fame even as Emrys feels hollow using momentum built on suspicion. Beat: success as moral test.

chapters.title: What My Mother Would Have Done
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Reading the notebook again, Emrys realizes her mother also misjudged someone she loved. Beat: compassion breaking through pride.

chapters.title: Finding Him at the Fence
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys finds Julian clearing debris from the condemned garden alone at night. Beat: quiet reconciliation without absolution yet.

chapters.title: The Real Date
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They go on one honest date — no rules, no contract — to a night market. Beat: joy, tentative and bright.

chapters.title: Zoning Board Showdown
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The public hearing on the garden's fate; testimony, threats, and Julian testifying against his own family. Beat: courage with stakes.

chapters.title: Father and Son
chapters.summary: Julian POV. A private scene between Julian and his father revealing the old man's own buried grief and corruption's origin. Beat: pity complicating anger.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Someone destroys the garden's irrigation the night before the final vote; suspicion falls on Ashfords. Beat: despair at the edge of victory.

chapters.title: Security Footage
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Julian finds footage implicating a rival developer who outbid his father — proof that could save or damn everything. Beat: moral crossroads.

chapters.title: Going Public
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They release the evidence together, exposing the rival and forcing the Ashford firm into retreat. Beat: solidarity forged in fire.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The council votes to preserve the garden as community land. Beat: catharsis and tears.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Apologies
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys visits her mother's grave, reading the notebook's last page aloud, finally forgiving them both. Beat: release.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Julian's father offers reinstatement and funding for the café — strings attached. Beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys declines the money; she'd rather owe the neighborhood than the empire. Beat: integrity as climax of character.

chapters.title: Community Ownership
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The café converts to a co-op; neighbors buy in with small sums. Beat: collective triumph.

chapters.title: First Frost Festival
chapters.summary: Both POVs. At the winter festival in the saved garden, Julian asks to start over — no contract this time. Beat: romantic climax.

chapters.title: The Answer Is a Tart
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys answers by baking him the tart from chapter eight, writing 'yes, slowly' in piped chocolate. Beat: tenderness earned.

chapters.title: Spring Planting
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later, they plant her mother's heirloom seeds together. Beat: renewal and continuity.

chapters.title: The Small Garden
chapters.summary: Emrys POV closing epilogue. One year on: café thriving, garden blooming, heart no longer contained but chosen. Final beat: peace — love as something grown, not guarded.
